contributions: C1: a learned importance score that prunes 3D Gaussians during training

overview:
A solid efficiency paper whose main speed claim holds, but the novelty of the pruning score is overstated.
C1 closely matches LightGaussian's global significance score; the paper cites LightGaussian but describes it as "heuristic, not learned", which the fact-check found inaccurate.
The 3DGS baseline PSNR in Table 1 (27.21) is lower than the original paper's 27.45 on the same split.
Two strong 2025 pruning methods are not cited or compared.
Fixing the baseline numbers and adding one ablation on the regularizer would address most major concerns.
summary: The paper proposes SparseSplat, which learns a per-Gaussian importance score during 3D Gaussian Splatting training and prunes low-importance Gaussians, combined with a view-dependent opacity regularizer. On Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks and Temples and Deep Blending it reports 3.1x faster rendering and 58% fewer Gaussians at comparable PSNR.

strengths.point: Clear and practically relevant goal: real-time rendering on consumer GPUs.
Speed measurements are thorough, reported on three GPUs with warm-up and variance.
Code and training configs are promised and hyperparameters are fully listed.

weaknesses.title: The learned importance score (C1) is close to LightGaussian's significance score
weaknesses.detail: LightGaussian [14] computes a global significance from hit count × opacity × volume, and its §3.2 also fine-tunes the score jointly with training. The claimed difference, that SparseSplat's score is learned, amounts to one extra MLP head. §2 describes [14] as a "heuristic, not learned" method, which understates the overlap.
weaknesses.suggestion: Reposition C1 as an extension of [14]. Add a direct comparison with [14] at matched Gaussian counts, and an ablation that replaces your score with [14]'s score inside your pipeline.

weaknesses.title: 3DGS baseline PSNR is lower than the original paper reports
weaknesses.detail: Table 1 lists 3DGS at 27.21 PSNR on Mip-NeRF 360. The original 3DGS paper reports 27.45 (its Table 1, same 7-scene split, 30k iterations). Most of the reported +0.18 dB gain of SparseSplat would disappear against the original number.
weaknesses.suggestion: Use the published 27.45 or explain the re-run setting (resolution, iterations, seed). Report mean ± std over 3 seeds for both methods.

weaknesses.title: No ablation isolating the opacity regularizer (C2)
weaknesses.detail: Table 4 ablates pruning thresholds but always keeps the regularizer on, so its contribution to quality and speed cannot be separated.
weaknesses.suggestion: Add rows with the regularizer removed and with it added to vanilla 3DGS.

weaknesses.title: Missing comparison to two 2025 pruning methods
weaknesses.detail: [U1] and [U2] report higher compression at equal PSNR on the same benchmarks and were public well before the deadline.
weaknesses.suggestion: Cite both and add them to Table 1, or explain why they are not comparable.

weaknesses.title: Fig. 4 y-axis starts at 26.5 dB
weaknesses.detail: The truncated axis makes a 0.2 dB gap look like a large margin.
weaknesses.suggestion: Start the axis at a round value or add a note that it is truncated.

verdicts.contribution: C1: learned importance score for pruning
verdicts.evidence: [14] §3.2 fine-tunes its significance score jointly with training, which is the core of C1.
[U3] uses a similar view-conditioned opacity penalty for anti-aliasing, not pruning.

verdicts.contribution: C3: 3.1x faster rendering at equal PSNR
verdicts.evidence: No prior work reports this speed at equal quality on these GPUs, though [U1] is close at 2.6x.

novelty.discussion: The strongest novelty is the **combination** of pruning with the opacity regularizer and the resulting speed. The importance score on its own is incremental over [LightGaussian](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17245).

questions: How was the 3DGS baseline in Table 1 trained, and why does it differ from the published 27.45 dB?
Does the importance score transfer to a pre-trained 3DGS model without retraining?
What is the training-time overhead of the extra MLP head?

revision_plan.step: Re-run or correct the 3DGS baseline in Table 1 and report 3 seeds for all methods.
Rewrite the description of LightGaussian in §2 and reposition C1 as an extension of it.
Add a regularizer ablation to Table 4.
Redraw Fig. 4 with an untruncated axis.

venue_form.value: The paper proposes SparseSplat, a 3DGS variant that learns a per-Gaussian importance score for pruning and adds a view-dependent opacity regularizer, reporting 3.1x faster rendering at comparable PSNR on three standard benchmarks.

1. Practically relevant goal with careful speed measurements (Table 3).
2. Full hyperparameters and promised code (Appendix B).

1. The learned importance score is close to LightGaussian's significance score, which the paper describes inaccurately (§2, §3.1).
2. The 3DGS baseline PSNR in Table 1 is below the published number on the same split.
3. No ablation isolates the opacity regularizer.
4. Two recent pruning methods are missing from the comparison.
The speed results are useful, but the novelty claim and the baseline numbers need correcting before the gains can be trusted.

reads.summary: Introduces 3D Gaussian Splatting: anisotropic 3D Gaussians optimized with adaptive density control and a tile-based differentiable rasterizer, reaching real-time rendering at state-of-the-art quality. Reports 27.45 PSNR on Mip-NeRF 360.

baseline_numbers.detail: Submission Table 1: 27.21. Original Table 1: 27.45, same split and iteration count.

reads.summary: Prunes Gaussians by a global significance score, distills spherical harmonics and applies vector quantization, reaching 15x compression and more than 200 FPS.

citation_accuracy.detail: Submission §2: "heuristic, not learned". [14] §3.2 fine-tunes the score jointly during training.

issues.claim: Described as "heuristic, not learned", but [14] fine-tunes the score during training.

verification.evidence: The score formula is hand-designed, but it is refined by training (§3.2), so "not learned" is overstated.
